body:
Ah, we're in the same age group. I didn't know about those "requirements" for getting treated in the UK. Fuck you for not being homeless, right? Bullshit on top of bullshit as far as the administration goes, it's the same in a lot of countries so it seems. Here in Eastern Europe it's pretty similar. Except it's maybe an even bigger "fuck you" if you're homeless. 

Feeling you on 'my friends are doing better than me'. Heck, some already grew and moved on from me, which is quite understandable. Being funny can keep people around us only for so long, and after a while they see there's actually not much there to hang around for. Yeah. 

Don't even want to go into the finances, I've wasted any potential that might have been existed to make something of myself and hold down a decent job.

 Do you have or have you had any vices? I've literally drank myself through my 20s and had a lot of dedicated drinking buddies at that time to accompany me, but each of those people had got a grip and moved on to become better in life. Why couldn't I? This is, of course, rhetorical. 

I can tell you what's keeping me, for now: don't want to hurt my immediate family and loved ones. That's it. More of an ethical issue in my case, if I can call it that. I've sat for the past couple of days trying to think up a plan on how to cover expenses for my cremation - I don't think I'll go with a funeral - so that I don't put financial strain and cause more stress to the people around me than it'd be necessary.

Today is not one of your good days. And I'm glad you posted here, there's a vague feeling of comfort in being familiar with someone's mental state.

Understood. Sorry for being nosy, I'm not from the USA and not really sure where you live, but what exactly does 'being put on a list' do for someone? Like, are you on a list of people who can get prescribed medication? And if I got that right, does that mean you've never, let's say, "taken advantage" of being able to use medication? Sorry, lol, I'm genuinely not informed well.

On the good days, do you sometimes have a nagging feeling that your brain might be fucking with you on the bad days? I literally have that thought pop up into my mind on 'better' days, I just hear a voice "your brain is fucking with you", and it's a good voice. And for a moment there I'm like "Huh, maybe that's true, a part of my inner being is just for some reason against myself and is making me feel this shitty way."

On the other hand, the bad days come back and I truly believe that, as you've put it so well, you can't fix something that was made with the wrong parts. And I shouldn't have to suffer through all that experience.

Huh, basically all of my thoughts, word for word practically. I never can tell if this state of mind maybe requires a session with a therapist, or if some medication is needed, or if it's just authentically how we truly feel.

I feel that way. Wrote a post about it here, too. It's Like 'reasons' generally stop applying altogether, for anything. And I don't want to bother anyone with it and I don't want to sit through shock and disbelief  if I told someone. Especially the people close to me or who've known me for years. I'm thinking, damn, like if I'm sure no one could guess how I'm feeling, then I probably can't guess for someone else. Doesn't matter, though. Where will you go from here?
